title: HildebrandHorstEds-2020-SeverelyInjuredPatient-MDPI
universal_lens: The structural unification of severely injured patient care relies on a multi-scale operator algebra. We define the state space as a Hilbert bundle over physiological manifolds, where diagnostic and therapeutic interventions act as bounded linear operators. The convergence of prehospital intubation success and postoperative renal biomarkers forms a unified spectral metric for systemic trauma resilience. Geriatric trauma injury dynamics integrate comorbidity, medication, and fall severity to predict mortality and quality of life outcomes.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps clinical trial outcomes to Bayesian posterior distributions over intervention efficacy. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed around first-pass intubation success rates and acute kidney injury incidence. This allows dynamic calibration of medical resource allocation under epistemic uncertainty, treating missing physiological data as latent variables in a hierarchical Dirichlet process. Bayesian inference models trauma risk factors (ISS, AIS, polypharmacy) to forecast mortality and HRQoL using probabilistic causal networks.
gse_mapping: GSE models the trauma resuscitation unit as a continuous-time Markov decision process. State transitions correspond to shifts in Glasgow Coma Scale or hemodynamic stability. Situational reasoning evaluates optimal control policies—such as videolaryngoscopy deployment or intraoperative CT usage—by maximizing the expected cumulative reward of long-term patient survival and minimizing iatrogenic complications. Situational reasoning maps injury mechanisms (falls, gait instability) to state transitions in mobility, self-care, and recovery trajectories.

primitives.name: Chest Trauma Mortality Metric
